I farm 8 mu, so I do not spread money around blindly. I start from what has worked for me in recent years around Quzhou. Wheat and maize both need to be steady on fertilizer and water if I want a safe yield. I have well irrigation, so I will lean on that instead of gambling on rain. On wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer down, and give it 3 irrigations if the year is normal: one after sowing if the soil is dry, one at greening or jointing, and one around grain filling. Wheat is where I do not dare to be short on nitrogen, because thin wheat in spring is hard to fix later. On maize after wheat, I will move fast so I do not miss moisture. I will use hybrid seed, keep the stand full, and put a solid amount of nitrogen because summer maize eats fertilizer fast. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose ears and grain weight. I will not go too fancy on tillage because I only have 8 mu and labor matters; rotary or direct sowing saves time and diesel. For pesticides, I will do what I usually do: wheat about 2 sprays, maize about 2 sprays, then add one more only if I really see pressure in the field. This way I keep yield stable without pushing costs too hard.
